newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close near the day's highs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close near the day's highs.

text.p: Swiss shares extended early gains near the end of the session to close more than one percent higher on Wednesday as the strong dollar and a favourable domestic interest rate outlook boosted the market, dealers said.
The blue-chip SMI index gained 82.8 points, or 1.42 percent, to end at 5,927.5. The broad Swiss Performance Index advanced 44.91 points, or 1.22 percent, to finish at 3,730.31.
Bourse volume was at 2.74 billion Swiss francs.

Among blue chips, Nestle rebounded from a period of prolonged weakness to close 17 francs higher at 1,968. Dealers said expectations were high ahead of half-year sales, which were due out on Thursday.
Roche profited from Tuesday's first half-year sales figures, which came in at the upper end of market expections, dealers said. Roche certificates soared 385 francs to 14,810.
Novartis registereds underperformed the market, advancing 24 francs to 2,441.
Derivatives transactions led to high volatility, dealers said.
Sulzer rebounded from recent lows, advancing 17 francs to 1,227. One trader said the share profited from the float of subsidiary Sulzer Medica on Monday.

Sulzer Medica was up 18.50 francs to 434.5. Sulzer Medica chief executive Andre Buchel said in a newspaper interview that the company would not wait long before making acquisitions in its core businesses.
Among financials, SBC, Credit Suisse and Swiss Re were among the biggest winners.

SBC was up eight francs at 418. On Tuesday it announced an alliance in the Japanese market with Japanese bank LTCB which includes taking stakes in each other and setting up three joint ventures. Dealers said the deal was favourable for SBC.
